transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I just can't shake this thought I've been having. I've been an electrician for years, and if all that time on the job couldn't keep my own brother safe... then I just feel like I'm a danger to anybody who works with me, or even the people living under my roof.
Can you describe what this thought is like? Do you find it coming into your mind over and over, even when you don't want it to?

Yeah, it comes into my mind a lot, even when I'm trying to focus on something else. But it's... it's more than just a passing thought. 

I'll be right in the middle of wiring a panel at work, or maybe I'll just hear my nephew shut the garage door at home, and suddenly I'm right back there. I can actually smell the smoke again, and I see my brother. It's like the real world, the job site I'm currently on, just completely drops out from under me.
Do these experiences feel like you're actually reliving the event, as if it’s happening all over again in the moment?

Yeah, exactly. It feels like it's happening right then and there. I'm not just remembering it, I'm... I'm back in that moment. My heart starts pounding, and I feel the same panic I felt that day. It's like I'm completely disconnected from whatever I was actually doing.
Can you tell me about the event that you keep reliving? Was it something that happened to you or someone close to you that felt life-threatening or caused serious harm?

Yeah, it was my brother. Like I mentioned before, we were working a job together. Um... I don't really know how to explain the whole thing right now, to be honest. But yeah, it was an accident on the site, and there was smoke. 

It was definitely life-threatening. He got hurt really badly. I just... I can't really go into all the specifics of exactly what went wrong that day, if that's okay. But yes, it was very serious, and it happened right in front of me.
Since the accident, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I don't go in my own garage anymore unless I absolutely have to. I used to volunteer doing electrical work for my church, but I quit doing that. And if anyone starts talking about car projects or... or the fire, I just shut it down fast. I can't be around that.
Since the accident, have you been feeling guilty, angry, or blaming yourself for what happened to your brother?

Yeah, I do. Honestly, there's just this heavy mix of guilt and anger sitting in my chest pretty much all day. It's... it's especially bad when I look at my nephew. I just look at him and think about how he lost his dad, and now he's stuck with me instead.
Since the accident, have you noticed that you’ve lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with family?

Um, no, not really. I mean, besides what I already said about avoiding the garage and quitting the electrical work... I still care about my family. I still spend time with them, and with my nephew. So, no, I haven't really lost interest in everything else. I still try to do normal things when I can.
Since the accident, have you found yourself being easily startled or feeling constantly on guard, like you're always watching for danger?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I don't jump at loud noises or feel like I'm constantly looking over my shoulder. I'm just dealing with... well, the guilt and staying away from the garage, like I said. But no, I wouldn't say I feel on guard all the time.
